ledger_contexts.statement: A smooth connected projective complex curve C of genus 21 has a line bundle L of degree 10, a fixed isomorphism L^4=K_C, a reduced six-point divisor Z, and basis r=xi*u of H0(C,L) with simple common divisor Z. Assume every hypothesis of prop:curve-data and prop:residue-data in the staged September-23-2026 manuscript, including evaluation surjectivity for all powers L^k with k>=3. In compatible coordinates at q_j, m_j=c_j/z_j with c_j nonzero, R_j=m_j*r and p_j=P-m_j*r' are holomorphic, P is a global meromorphic L^2 row with only the stated simple poles, p_j(0) wedge R_j(0)=1, and sum_j(R_j(0) wedge R_j'(0)-1)=-90. The rows r'(q_j) span C^2.

supplied_geometric_hypotheses: Smooth connected projective complex C, deg L=10, fixed L^4=K_C, reduced six-point simple common divisor Z of a basis r of H0(L).
h0(L)=h0(L(Z))=2, h0(O_C)=h0(O_C(Z))=1; derivative rows r'(q_j) span C^2; a pencil member r_1 has four further reduced zeros disjoint from Z.
One global P in H0(C,L^2(Z))^2, not independent local rows; m_j=c_j/z_j with c_j nonzero, R_j=m_j r and p_j=P-m_j r' holomorphic.
p_j(0) wedge R_j(0)=1 and sum_j(R_j(0) wedge R_j'(0)-1)=-90=-9 deg L.
Evaluation of every L^k, k>=3, at Z is supplied by the upstream proposition and is also derived here from the section counts and negative-degree duality.

claim_assessments.ledger_statement: For D=t^k(b E_t+h d_z) and V=t^(ell+1)(A E_t+B d_z), [D,V] has the coefficients displayed in jets:general-bracket; div_sigma(D)=t^k((k-4)b+h'). The leading action is delta A_k=(1-k)br+hr', delta B_k=-khr.
claim_assessments.reason: Direct ordinary-coordinate differentiation gives the full bracket and weighted divergence with the manuscript signs. The historical exact checker derives these rather than assuming the logarithmic formula.

claim_assessments.ledger_statement: Under the exact curve and residue hypotheses, after determinant-normalized horizontal matching by volume-preserving order-one and order-two flows, all four duality tests for the order-two vertical class in H1(C,L^3)^2 vanish.
claim_assessments.reason: The complete residue matrix is evaluated. Global residues of P_i P_j kill every symmetric entry, and the alternating part equals the outside total by sum(W_j-1)=-9 deg L. Thus all four tests, including both diagonal tests, vanish.

claim_assessments.ledger_statement: For the data of prop:curve-data and prop:residue-data, finite compositions of holomorphic overlap flows of orders 1,...,7 fix C and its conormal L and admit rows A_k,B_k for 0<=k<=7 matching through index seven with A wedge B=t^2(1+O(t)). On a realization they give sections of I F/I^9 F with leading determinant t^4 E_t wedge d_z=t^5 d_t wedge d_z.
claim_assessments.reason: Stop the simultaneous induction at k=7 and realize only the finitely many overlap flows as holomorphic germs. Row index seven means logarithmic coefficient degree eight and matching modulo I^9 F. A realization and lifting to actual analytic fields are not supplied here.

claim_assessments.ledger_statement: For the fixed volume-preserving first two steps, the four vertical obstruction tests equal epsilon_ij times (sum_j(W_j-1)+9 deg L)/12; the symmetric tests vanish by the global residue theorem for P_i P_j.
claim_assessments.reason: Including the half-second-bracket term gives T coefficients -7/12,-3/4,-5/4,-17/12. Its symmetric part is -2/3 Res(P_i P_j dz), and its alternating part is epsilon_ij(R wedge p+R wedge R')/12. Inside and outside totals both equal [[0,-15/2],[15/2,0]]. The conclusion requires the single global P.

claim_assessments.ledger_statement: After interpolating A_2 and incorporating the old order-one transition, adding lambda_j/z_j to h_3 and 3 lambda_j r/z_j to the disk B_3 preserves all equations through determinant degree three and changes the vertical obstruction by 3 sum_j lambda_j r'(q_j); this map is surjective.
claim_assessments.reason: The disk compensation is holomorphic, cancels the transition's horizontal change, and wedges to zero with r. Its remaining canonical residue is 3 lambda_j r'(q_j); a nonzero two-row minor supplies an explicit right inverse. Degree-four determinant terms may change because that equation has not yet been imposed; step-four interpolation of A_3 handles them.

claim_assessments.ledger_statement: After simultaneous field matching at order four, the degree-four determinant-target obstruction is represented by -dh_4. The leading order-four horizontal generator is an intrinsic scalar, and each contour residue of this exact differential is zero.
claim_assessments.reason: The transformation h_tilde=g^(4-k)h makes h_4 scalar and -h_4' dz a canonical exact differential. The vertical generator's divergence coefficient vanishes at k=4. Earlier flows preserve sigma and affect this leading order only from degree five onward; single-valued holomorphy suffices for zero contour integrals.

claim_assessments.ledger_statement: With targets compatible two determinant degrees ahead of imposed equations, interpolation of A_(k-1), horizontal matching, vertical splitting and target extension work for every k>=3. For k>=4 the vertical obstruction vanishes, and for k>=5 the target obstruction vanishes by negative-degree Serre duality. Every fixed field coefficient stabilizes after the following step.
claim_assessments.reason: Evaluation cokernel dual is H0(L^(4-k)(Z))/H0(L^(4-k)); counts settle k=3,4 and degree <=-4 settles all k>=5. Old first-transition terms ((k-1)m'a/3+ma',-ma) are included. Vertical dual L^(3-k) vanishes for k>=4; target dual L^(4-k) for k>=5. Targets use exp(D-div_sigma D), including earlier-target contributions. A_n is last modified at step n+1; the remaining objects stabilize at their own steps.

claim_assessments.ledger_statement: For every data set satisfying the stated curve and residue hypotheses of prop:jets, and every integer N>=2, there exist compatible overlap transitions and field rows through index N with A wedge B=t^2(1+O(t)). In fact the coupled construction has a coefficientwise stable formal limit with determinant target G sigma^-1. This is a conditional existence theorem, not an analytic convergence or algebraization theorem.
claim_assessments.reason: Finite stopping and coefficientwise formal stabilization follow from the assessed induction. The empty external-assumption list does not remove the proof's reliance on Serre duality and Cartan B; later versions make those inputs explicit. No convergence or input-existence conclusion is justified.

claim_assessments.ledger_statement: On each Stein chart and overlap, coherent analytic sheaves have zero positive cohomology (Cartan B); the resulting acyclic cover computes the first cohomology used in the Cousin splittings.
claim_assessments.reason: The original page image confirms q>=1 despite OCR q>1. A very ample multiple of Z embeds C minus Z as a closed smooth affine subvariety; the charts/intersections are Stein and the bundles/kernels coherent. The resulting cover is acyclic for the Cousin splittings and local lifting problems.

claim_assessments.ledger_statement: A holomorphic vector field vanishing along a divisor has a time-one holomorphic flow germ, with inverse, after restricting transversely over a compact subannulus; finite compositions realize their Taylor series.
claim_assessments.reason: For the actual generators, transverse scaling makes the vector fields and first derivatives O(epsilon^k) on a slightly larger annulus; local holomorphic Picard iteration supplies time plus/minus one and a common transverse restriction for finitely many flows. The general local vanishing-field statement also follows by finite time subdivision in the local ODE theorem. No global completeness, Hausdorff realization, or infinite analytic composition follows.

external_assumptions.statement: For a smooth compact complex curve and holomorphic line bundle B, H1(C,B)^*=H0(C,K_C tensor B^-1); the pairing is cup product followed by trace. Contour representatives are derived separately.
external_assumptions.ledger_statement: For a compact complex manifold X and holomorphic vector bundle V, Serre duality pairs H^q(X,Omega^p(V)) perfectly with H^(n-q)(X,Omega^(n-p)(V*)). For a smooth compact curve this gives H1(C,B)=H0(C,K_C tensor B^-1)^*.
external_assumptions.locator: Serre, Un theoreme de dualite (1955), section 3 no.13 Theorem 4 p.22, no.15 p.23; section 4 no.16 Theorem 5 and corollary p.24
external_assumptions.passage: Theorem 5 pairs H^q(X,Omega^p(D)) with H^(n-q)(X,Omega^(n-p)(-D)) on a compact complex manifold. Its corollary pairs H^q(X,L(D)) with H^(n-q)(X,L(K-D)). No.15 identifies the pairing as cup product followed by top-cohomology trace.
